members.thesis: This strategy trades based on index momentum. weaknesses: Only works if stock is highly correlated with index; idiosyncratic moves break the setup

members.name: index_momentum_stock_selection_v1
members.thesis: When Nifty50 has strong intraday momentum (return from open > 0.5% by 10:00), the highest-beta stocks in the index tend to amplify this move for the rest of the day. By going long the top 5 highest-beta Nifty50 stocks on bullish index days (and short top 5 on bearish days), you lever up the index mo
filters: all 5 stocks must have > SMA(volume, 20) by 10:00
skip if any stock has spread > 0.1%
weaknesses: 5 simultaneous positions = 5x brokerage cost (₹200 just for entry)
Beta estimates are backward-looking — a stock's beta today may differ from its 20-day historical beta
On index reversal days, all 5 stocks reverse together = correlated losses
members.prior_art: Beta-momentum strategy — factor investing concept applied intraday

members.name: index_constituent_spread_v1
members.thesis: When a Nifty50 constituent deviates significantly from the index's intraday move (stock return vs beta-adjusted index return), it tends to converge. This is because index-level buying/selling (via ETFs and index futures) creates uniform pressure on all constituents, but execution lags cause some sto
filters: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
skip if stock volume < 50% of 20-bar avg
weaknesses: This is a single-leg trade (not hedged with index) so you have directional risk if index moves
Beta estimation error on rolling 20-day window can cause false residual signals
On stock-specific news days, the residual is driven by genuine information, not mean-reverting flow
members.prior_art: Index vs constituent spread trading — used by index arbitrage desks globally
